/-!
# Erdős Problem 476

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/476](https://www.erdosproblems.com/476)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
- [dSHa94] Dias da Silva, J. A. and Hamidoune, Y. O., *Cyclic spaces for Grassmann
  derivatives and additive theory*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1994), 140-146.
-/

namespace Erdos476

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$. Let
$$
A\hat{+}A = \{ a+b : a\neq b \in A\}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
\lvert A\hat{+}A\rvert \geq \min(2\lvert A\rvert-3,p)?
$$

This is the Erdős-Heilbronn inequality, proved by Dias da Silva and Hamidoune.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos476.lean"]
theorem erdos_476 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, Fact p.Prime → ∀ A : Finset (ZMod p),
      A.restrictedSumset.card ≥ min (2 * A.card - 3) p := by
  sorry

end Erdos476

reformulations.difference: Lean uses natural-number subtraction in the lower bound and quantifies over all Finsets, including the empty set. The literature uses ordinary subtraction and sometimes explicitly requires a nonempty subset.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For |A| ≥ 2, natural and integer subtraction agree. For |A| = 0 or 1, truncation replaces a negative lower bound by zero; both inequalities hold because cardinalities are nonnegative. The additional empty-set case is therefore harmless. For prime p, ZMod p is the field with p elements, so every subset is represented by a Finset. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, full_statement_equivalence and nonempty_source_equivalence prove the quantified equivalences to set-based statements with integer arithmetic, without using the sorry-backed problem theorem. Their axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

review.notes:
The sole declaration faithfully states the Erdős–Heilbronn inequality. Erdős–Graham p. 95 explicitly asks for distinct pair sums to occupy at least 2|A|−3 residue classes, or all p classes when that bound exceeds p. The accepted 1994 proof and the public problem database support research solved and answer(True).

Checked restricted-sumset membership and deduplication, the prime guard, and all small boundary cases. Exhaustive Lean evaluations passed for every subset with p = 2, 3, 5, 7, and 11. The external proof's definition was proved equivalent to the repository definition. After tactic-only compatibility edits in a scratch copy of the linked v4.29.1 proof, /workspace/review/exact-statement-proof.lean proves the exact repository statement on the local toolchain, with only standard axioms.

Access limitations: erdosproblems.com/476 and its forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers. The original Dias da Silva–Hamidoune full text and Guy's full chapter were unavailable; the claim was settled against the accessible primary Erdős–Graham text and the author-hosted Alon–Nathanson–Ruzsa paper, which states the exact theorem and credits the 1994 proof. No repository files were edited.
